topic.title: Instagram is testing a homescreen with no photos on it
topic.claim: Instagram quietly testing a homescreen that opens straight into Reels instead of photos is the company finally admitting what it already knows about what you actually watch.
topic.behaviour: Meta is piloting a redesigned Instagram in India and South Korea where users land directly on a Reels feed, with a new bottom bar ordering Home, Reels, Stories, DMs and Profile, and three feed tabs called All, Friends and Latest.
topic.mechanism: India has the biggest short-video audience Instagram has anywhere, built on the back of the 2020 TikTok ban, and app design always follows where the attention already is, not where the company wants it to be.
topic.group: Instagram users and creators who still post photo carousels
real_details: Test markets are India and South Korea
New bottom bar order: Home, Reels, Stories, DMs, Profile
Three feed tabs: All, Friends, Latest
topic.news_peg: TechCrunch report on Meta's Reels-first homescreen test, October 6, 2026
topic.why_now: The test just leaked and is being discussed by creators this month

score.why: A named platform quietly admitting what it already knows about its own users, sharp and plain, no sociology detour.

topic.send_to: the friend who says they only open Instagram to check messages

edits: slide 6: cut 'The test just moves the furniture to where everyone was already sitting.' It repeats the slide's first line, and the last line of slide 9 makes the same point.

paragraphs: We all say we open Instagram to see our friends. Then we spend forty minutes watching a stranger redo a kitchen. Meta noticed.
Swipe to read →
Meta announced the test for a limited group of users in India. South Korea got it too.
You open the app and you land in Reels. Your friends' photos come later.
The swipe is the front door now.
The rest of the layout says the same thing.
Reels moves up to the second tab. DMs move to the centre of the bar, right where your thumb rests.
Everything else shuffles around those two.

Even the feed got split three ways:
– All, for recommended posts and reels
– Friends, for mutuals
– Latest, for the newest
Friends is now a tab you tap into. The people you followed for years are a filter now.
And honestly, Meta isn't guessing.
I open Instagram to reply to one message. Forty minutes later I'm watching a stranger renovate a kitchen in Pune.
I never scrolled back to see a single friend's photo.
Apps don't decide where your attention goes. They follow it.
India has over 300 million Instagram users. A lot of them are already swiping.
The old feed was people you chose. This one is whoever keeps you there longest.
Your cousin's wedding photos now compete with a stranger doing a trend in Goa.
Which brings me to this post. A carousel. Slow, made of words, asking you to stop.
On an app testing a front door built for the opposite.
Every carousel creator is checking their reach nervously, and so am I.
For brands, the hint is plain.
If your plan still starts with a pretty grid, you're building for a tab people have to go looking for.

hook_candidates.hook: We all say we open Instagram to see our friends. Then we spend forty minutes watching a stranger redo a kitchen. Meta noticed.
Instagram is testing an app in India that opens straight into Reels. Your friends' photos now come after strangers. Here's what Meta knows.
Instagram's front door in India is now a stranger's Reel. Your friends got moved to a tab you have to tap into.
I have a prediction. Soon you'll open Instagram and won't see one friend's photo unless you go looking for it.
Meta calls opening Instagram into Reels a small test in India. It's really built on what your thumb already does every night.

sources.fact: TechCrunch reported on September 29, 2025 that Instagram was testing a Reels-first interface in India and South Korea. The report does not match the October 6, 2026 date given in the news peg. The article describes DMs in the center of the bottom bar and three feed tabs: All, Friends and Latest.
